title: Reject stale plan approvals with an expectedPlanRevision on approve
description: MoeCommandSender.approveTask(taskId) sends only the task id, and the daemon approve path (taskStore / WebSocketServer) checks status, not which plan revision the human saw. The JetBrains PlanReviewDialog builds DoD and steps once and rerenders only comments on later updates, so a newer submit_plan can be approved from a dialog still showing the old plan. Add a monotonically increasing plan revision to the task (bumped on every submit_plan), accept expectedPlanRevision on the approve command (WS message from the plugins and the MCP tool if one exists), reject with a structured error when it does not match the current revision, and make the JetBrains dialog either rerender the plan on a revision change or disable Approve with a 'plan changed — refresh' notice. VS Code: send the revision too (small). Source: roadmap 2026-09-10 §4 'Fix approval freshness'.
definitionOfDone: task.planRevision exists in docs/SCHEMA.md and is bumped by submit_plan (vitest)
Approve with a stale expectedPlanRevision returns a structured error and leaves the task in AWAITING_APPROVAL (vitest); approve without the field keeps working for old clients
JetBrains PlanReviewDialog sends expectedPlanRevision and cannot approve a plan it has not rendered (JUnit test on the dialog model or presenter)
VS Code approve command sends expectedPlanRevision
./gradlew test and daemon npm test green

implementationPlan.description: VERIFY SIX DELIVERIES AND DE-CONFLICT OWNERSHIP. Read-only, no edits. This parent is the final integration gate over the original five Definition-of-Done items; it is NOT a re-implementation and must not duplicate a single line of child work. (a) For each of the six children prove actual landing, not status: epicSiblings landing.merged true, or `git log <branch> --grep "Moe-Task: <childId>"` finds a commit. The ids are task-492b573920264188888d56638dd98d81 (daemon revision producer, ALREADY LANDED at 7da080b), task-dd743a02000e46cca6ae2442a1821066 (daemon compare-and-swap), task-0ad3744e77bd43b08b9c0b63293912a6 (JetBrains model and wire), task-247fdf296ff2445daae8e057c0608f51 (JetBrains dialog binding), task-34dba87e4e1948bcba69e85f3f34bfd3 (VS Code model and wire), task-1bf079020e504aaaa760a8faeddebbcd (VS Code panel binding). A DONE column, a dirty working tree or a peer's uncommitted bytes are NOT evidence. If any is unlanded, moe.report_blocked naming the specific unmet ids rather than filling the gap here. (b) Record the delivered contract verbatim rather than assuming it, because these names are what the integration test asserts: the numeric refusal code and its codeName, the exact spelling of the error detail keys, where the token rides on each wire message, and the presenter or model type each client uses to freeze its rendered revision. Note one known wart to document rather than change: the producer's exhaustion error already ships detail key `currentRevision`, while the compare-and-swap slice uses `currentPlanRevision`, so a client parsing both sees two spellings. (c) De-conflict file ownership. The compare-and-swap child owns the approval section of docs/MCP_SERVER.md and will have landed it first; this parent VERIFIES and corrects that text against delivered code, it does not rewrite it. The runtime already flagged that collision, so re-read the landed version before touching the file. Likewise docs/SCHEMA.md carries the producer's planRevision section. (d) Re-measure `git status`, list every foreign dirty path in the step note and preserve all of them. (e) Build an explicit map from each of the five original Definition-of-Done items to the child test that proves it, so the new integration test adds only the cross-layer cases no single child could own. No builds, no full regression in this step.

CROSS-LAYER INTEGRATION TEST. Explicit error handling coverage is the point of this step: every refusal, malformed token, disconnected client and teardown path gets an asserted outcome. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/server/planApproval.integration.test.ts using the real-dispatch pattern already established in src/server/WebSocketServer.test.ts and the compare-and-swap child's planApproval.test.ts: a real http server on port 0, a real StateManager over a disposable temp project, a real McpAdapter and real ws clients, under CONTROL approval mode. Never call a private handler directly and never race two direct calls; anything not driven over a socket goes through state.runExclusive, which is how production reaches the store. The cases here are the ones NO single child could own, so do not re-run a child's whole matrix: a review client A snapshots revision N over the plugin socket while client B submits a newer plan over the MCP socket, and A's later approval at N is refused with the exact code, codeName and detail keys recorded in step 1, leaving the task AWAITING_APPROVAL with unchanged persisted bytes, timestamps, assignment, activity and no approval event; A then refreshes to N+1 and approves successfully. Repeat that shape for the OTHER two writers the centralized stamp covers, since only an integration test crosses them: a real amend_plan_step, and a real plugin UPDATE_TASK edit of steps or the Definition of Done. Prove the one-bump rule end to end - both surfaces changed in one write advances once, a byte-identical full resubmit advances once, an equal sanitized edit and a comments-only change advance not at all. Prove durability by reloading a fresh StateManager and approving with the reloaded revision. Prove backwards compatibility: an omitted token still approves, and a legacy record with no stored stamp approves at explicit 0. Cover both approval routes, a malformed present token, a forged revision inside an update patch, and a serialized newer-submit-before-older-approval race. Assert observable refusal and state, never source ordering or a helper only the test calls. Red proof: revert the fence or the bump in an ISOLATED SCRATCH COPY outside the shared checkout, record which cases fail, and restore it before the gate - never mutate the shared tree, which peers are working in. In afterEach or finally, close every ws client, close the server, cancel timers and remove only the test-owned temp directory, on every operating system.

DOCUMENT THE FEATURE, CORRECT THE CONTRACT DOCS. Create docs/PLAN_APPROVAL_FRESHNESS.md as the one cross-client, user-visible note this feature has: what changed and why, plus a deterministic reproduction checklist a human can run - open the JetBrains review at revision N, change steps or the Definition of Done to N+1 WITHOUT touching comments, observe approve latched disabled with the close-and-reopen notice, reopen and review N+1; in VS Code, a click queued at N during the render debounce never silently upgrades to an unseen N+1, and the token advances only after a completed render. Include the recovery paths: stale refusal, disconnected service, failed render, same-revision comment updates, deleted task and a status that moved off AWAITING_APPROVAL. State the boundaries plainly so the doc does not promise universal fencing: an omitted token is still a legal legacy approval, the other board and detail approval entry points deliberately stay token-free, automatic SPEED and TURBO approval policy is unchanged, and a SPEED callback already queued behind the mutex can still fire after a human refusal. Then treat docs/SCHEMA.md and docs/MCP_SERVER.md as VERIFY-AND-CORRECT, not rewrite: the producer child owns the SCHEMA planRevision section and the compare-and-swap child owns the MCP_SERVER approval section, so read the landed text and fix only what the delivered code contradicts, noting the two error-detail-key spellings found in step 1 rather than renaming either. Map all five original parent Definition-of-Done items to the child test or integration case that proves each. If code and docs disagree in a way a doc edit cannot honestly fix, report it as a prerequisite defect instead of spreading implementation edits into child-owned source files.

ONE FULL FEATURE GATE, RUN FRESH AFTER THE TESTS AND DOCS ARE FINAL. From the repository root on Windows run exactly: cmd /d /c "npm --prefix packages/moe-daemon test && cd moe-jetbrains && gradlew.bat test && cd .. && npm --prefix moe-vscode test && npm --prefix moe-vscode run compile". On macOS or Linux: npm --prefix packages/moe-daemon test && (cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test) && npm --prefix moe-vscode test && npm --prefix moe-vscode run compile. That covers daemon vitest, the primary JetBrains JUnit suite, the secondary VS Code native tests and the TypeScript compile. Require exit 0, nonzero counts from all three suites, and confirm the new integration file was actually collected rather than silently skipped. Daemon vitest output on this box is buried in logger noise, so filter for the summary lines but capture the exit code in a separate statement, because a filtered pipeline swallows it. Gradle output is shared infrastructure here: serialize it through the Moe resource protocol if another agent owns it, and never kill a peer process or clean a shared cache. Record the exact command, exit code and output tail with counts for the verification argument of moe.complete_task, alongside each child's focused red-on-old proof. An unrun command, an uncollected test, a missing build prerequisite or an unrelated suite failure is an honest incomplete gate and must be reported as such, not smoothed over by rebuilding generated assets or widening ownership.

WHOLE-FEATURE ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, THEN HAND OFF. Review the six child diffs plus this integration and docs diff as one feature, not six. Confirm or fix: the counter never regresses and never double-bumps, and a sanitized no-op really is a no-op across every writer including amendment and the plugin update route; the daemon comparison happens under the real mutex and before any timer cancellation or write, so a refusal leaves bytes, cache, timestamps, assignment, activity and the pending SPEED timer untouched; no forged stamp or command metadata is persisted from any client; the refusal code, codeName and detail keys are identical in the daemon, both clients and the docs, and the numeric domain matches between the daemon's safe integer and Kotlin's Long with no narrowing to Int anywhere; JetBrains invalidates before the comments-equality early return and before the 200ms debounce, and its action-time recheck never substitutes a newer cached revision; VS Code's token comes from a completed render rather than the latest client state, and a click queued at N never becomes an approval at N+1; both clients refuse to approve while disconnected, on a deleted task or on a changed status, send at most once per click, keep the dialog usable on a send failure or daemon error, and leave no listener or timer behind on disposal; an omitted token still works for old clients; and no child test was weakened or deleted to make this gate pass. Verify the five original Definition-of-Done items are each satisfied by named evidence. If the review forces a code change, re-run the full gate on those final bytes before claiming success. Report every path actually created or modified in complete_step.modifiedFiles and attribute no foreign work in progress. Finish through moe.complete_task with the fresh verification evidence and an explicit checklist for QA; never mark the task DONE yourself.

comments.content:
Re-planned as instructed (architect-8b93cc67, 2026-09-11). Submitted, TURBO auto-approved: 5 steps, 4 distinct files, 2 new. Same shape and same four-file scope as the previous plan, because that scope was correct.

One correction to the record, stated rather than argued: the reopen reason says the prior five-step plan "predates the six-way decomposition". It does not. It was submitted at 2026-09-10T18:32:23Z, after the 18:24Z governor ruling, and it already carried all six child ids in dependsOn, named the same four parent-owned files, and cited the ruling in its planning notes. Nothing about it was stale in that sense.

The re-plan was still worth doing, for a different and real reason. When that plan was written none of the six children had delivered, so it could only describe the contract abstractly. Since then the producer landed (7da080b) and the daemon compare-and-swap plan is approved and in flight, which settles the concrete names the integration test has to assert and creates a genuine ownership overlap the runtime flagged as a file collision on docs/MCP_SERVER.md. So this version sharpens three things and changes nothing else:

1. Step 1 now names what to read off each delivery (refusal code, codeName, exact detail-key spellings, where the token rides on each wire message, which presenter or model type each client uses) instead of assuming it, and it blocks on specific unmet ids rather than filling gaps.
2. Step 3 becomes verify-and-correct rather than rewrite. The compare-and-swap child writes the MCP_SERVER approval section and lands first; the producer owns the SCHEMA planRevision section. The parent reads the landed text and fixes only what delivered code contradicts. docs/PLAN_APPROVAL_FRESHNESS.md stays the parent's own file.
3. Step 2 is scoped to only the cross-layer cases no single child can own: two sockets, three different writers of the revision, and the durability/legacy paths. It explicitly does not re-run any child's full matrix, and its red proof is taken in an isolated scratch copy, never the shared checkout peers are working in.

One inconsistency found and deliberately documented rather than fixed: the producer's shipped PLAN_REVISION_EXHAUSTED error uses detail key currentRevision, while the compare-and-swap slice uses currentPlanRevision. A client parsing both revision errors meets two spellings. Renaming a shipped, QA-approved key that downstream parsers bind to is a break, so step 1 records it and step 3 documents it.

Dependencies are unchanged: 5 of 6 still unmet, which correctly gates any WORKING claim.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Rewriting the parent plan from scratch - rejected: the existing five steps map cleanly to the five original Definition-of-Done items and the four-file scope is right; a rewrite would discard good work and churn the board. (2) Folding the parent's integration test into the compare-and-swap child - rejected: that child is daemon-only, while the cases that matter here cross MCP and plugin sockets, three different writers and two IDE clients. (3) Having the parent own the MCP_SERVER approval section outright - rejected: the compare-and-swap child writes it first and the runtime already flags the collision, so the parent verifies and corrects instead. (4) Renaming the producer's currentRevision detail key for symmetry - rejected: it is shipped and QA-approved, downstream parsers bind to it, and a late rename is a break; document both spellings. (5) Blocking the re-plan on the inaccurate reopen premise - rejected: the action requested is correct on its merits, so it proceeds, with the premise corrected in a task comment rather than argued about.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Re-planned 2026-09-11 by a second architect. The stated reason for the reopen does not survive checking: the prior five-step plan was submitted at 2026-09-10T18:32:23Z, AFTER the 18:24Z decomposition ruling, and already carries all six child ids in dependsOn with the same four parent-owned files. It did not predate the decomposition. The re-plan is still worth doing, for a different and real reason: when that plan was written none of the six children had delivered, so it could only describe the contract in the abstract. One child has since landed (producer, 7da080b) and the compare-and-swap child's plan is approved and in flight, which settles the concrete names the integration test must assert and creates a genuine ownership overlap on docs/MCP_SERVER.md that the runtime flagged as a file collision. This version therefore keeps the prior plan's five-step shape and four-file scope deliberately - it was sound work - and sharpens three things: prerequisite verification now names what to read off each delivery instead of assuming it; the docs step becomes verify-and-correct against child-owned sections rather than a rewrite; and the integration test is scoped to only the cross-layer cases no single child could own. One inconsistency worth documenting rather than fixing: the producer's shipped exhaustion error uses detail key currentRevision while the compare-and-swap slice uses currentPlanRevision, so a client parsing both revision errors meets two spellings.
planningNotes.risks: Five of six dependencies are unmet, four children are in flight and one is still planning, so this cannot be claimed for work yet - dependsOn gates the WORKING claim, which is exactly right. Nothing in this plan may be executed against contracts that have not landed; step 1 blocks instead of guessing. docs/MCP_SERVER.md is a live collision with the in-flight compare-and-swap child: read the landed version before editing or the parent will clobber it. Do not re-run each child's full test matrix in the integration file - it doubles the suite and creates two places to update. The red proof must be taken in an isolated scratch copy: peers are working in this shared checkout and a reverted fence there would corrupt their runs. Gradle output is shared infrastructure; serialize it. The full gate spans three package managers and a JVM toolchain, so a missing prerequisite must be reported as an incomplete gate rather than hidden. Finally, do not let the parent become a place to fix child defects: a contradiction between delivered code and the documented contract is a prerequisite defect to report, not something to paper over in prose.
